episodes.subject: c
episodes.title: First programs and representations
episodes.description: Read assignments, decode notation and reason about integer conversions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I'm Maya, and this is CSQuest Audio. Today, Leo and I are taking on First programs and representations.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: read assignments, decode notation and reason about integer conversions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with how programs change state and work our way to casts and integer division.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Can you walk me through how programs change state?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A C program describes a sequence of operations. Variables hold values; assignment changes a value. A hosted program starts in main and can write to standard output.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Statement means an instruction ending in a semicolon.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: int boxes = 3; boxes = boxes + 2; printf("%d", boxes); writes 5.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The assignment keeps the new value for the next statement.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to your first C program. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An initializer supplies a starting value; assignment replaces it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Variable means a named object holding a value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which function starts a hosted C program?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hosted execution calls main.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Positional notation gives each digit a weight. Binary uses powers of two; hexadecimal uses powers of sixteen. C integer constants use 0x for hexadecimal and a leading 0 for octal.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Binary means base two notation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The octal constant 012 means 1 × 8 + 2 = 10, not decimal twelve.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Keep numeric value separate from the notation used to write it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Hexadecimal means base sixteen notation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: What is the value of hexadecimal digit A?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hexadecimal extends decimal digits with A through F for ten through fifteen.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 10.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain representation practice to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Multiply each digit by its place value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Octal constant means an integer token with a leading zero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which token means decimal sixteen?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 0x10 is sixteen; 010 is octal eight; 0x16 is decimal twenty-two.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Unsigned arithmetic is reduced modulo one more than the maximum value. Signed overflow is undefined behavior. Small integer types can be promoted before an expression is evaluated.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Promotion means conversion to int or unsigned int for arithmetic.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: What is guaranteed for INT_MAX + 1 in type int?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Do not infer a portable result from one compiler run.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose No defined result: signed overflow.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Integer promotions happen before many operators. If int can hold every value of a small type, it becomes int. Mixed int and unsigned int arithmetic of equal rank instead converts the int to unsigned int.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Modulo means wrap within the unsigned range.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Assume unsigned char is 8 bits and int represents 0..255. With unsigned char x=255, x+1 is int 256, not byte zero.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Only a later conversion back to unsigned char reduces the value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We also need to talk about mixed integer comparisons.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Apply integer promotions and the usual arithmetic conversions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Signed overflow means a result outside its type range, with no defined result.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Assume int can represent 0..255. What is the type of unsigned char x plus int 1?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The unsigned char promotes to int before addition.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: In an explicitly assumed two's-complement width, a negative value has the modulo-2^width bit pattern. The highest bit has negative weight. This representation model does not make signed overflow defined.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For an 8-bit two's-complement diagram, -5 has pattern 11111011: 256-5=251 as an unsigned interpretation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Its signed interpretation is 251-256=-5.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: It does not make undefined C behavior valid.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Converting values changes their type and can change their value. Integer division discards the fractional part toward zero; floating division retains a fraction. A cast must occur before division if you want floating arithmetic.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Cast means an explicit type conversion.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which expression computes 7 divided by 2 with a fractional result?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Casting an operand before division causes floating arithmetic.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose (double)7 / 2.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave first programs and representations, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A C program describes a sequence of operations. Variables hold values; assignment changes a value. A hosted program starts in main and can write to standard output.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Converting values changes their type and can change their value. Integer division discards the fractional part toward zero; floating division retains a fraction. A cast must occur before division if you want floating arithmetic.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Take a small example of how programs change state and work it out before looking at the explanation. Then compare your reasoning.

episodes.subject: c
episodes.title: Control flow and expressions
episodes.description: Choose branches, trace loops and sequence side effects safely.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Maya and Leo here. Our section today is Control flow and expressions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: choose branches, trace loops and sequence side effects safely.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with choose with if and else and work our way to expression repair.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to choose with if and else. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A condition chooses which statements execute. Zero is false; any nonzero scalar value is true. An if/else selects one branch, while switch transfers to a matching case label and can fall through.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Condition means a test selecting a path.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: With int x=7; if(x>5) x+=2; else x-=2; x becomes 9.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A case without break continues into the following statements.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: switch and fall-through.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: switch jumps to the matching integer case label. It then executes sequentially, so a missing break can intentionally or accidentally fall through. default handles unmatched values.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Case means a label inside switch.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which statement compares a reading with zero?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: == tests equality; = performs assignment.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose reading == 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A loop condition is tested at a particular point.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Loops repeat a body while a condition holds. A for loop runs initialization once, then test, body and update. A do/while tests after the body, so it executes at least once.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Iteration means one pass through a loop body.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: for(int i=0;i<3;i++) total+=2; adds two three times. continue in a for loop still reaches its update expression.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A skipped body does not perform its update.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Test before each while/for body; test after each do body.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Continue means skip to the next iteration step.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A while condition is false initially. How often does its body run?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A while loop tests before the body.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with Zero times.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack control-flow challenges next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Apply continue or break before deciding which statements still run.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Accumulator means a running total.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: continue in a for loop moves next to…

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The loop update still runs on continue.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us The update expression, then the condition.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Operators combine values. Precedence determines grouping, not general operand evaluation order. Bitwise operators manipulate individual bits; logical operators test truth and yield zero or one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Precedence means how an expression is grouped.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A result must be masked bit by bit. Which operator is appropriate?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: & operates on individual bits; && is a truth test.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Precedence groups an expression; it does not generally specify the order in which operands are evaluated.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Distinguish logical && and || from bitwise & and |.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Mask means a bit pattern selecting bits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: 6 & 3 is 2 because 110 AND 011 = 010.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 6 && 3 is 1 because both operands are nonzero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with conditional and comma operators. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Side effects need a defined sequencing relationship. && and || evaluate left first and may skip right. The comma operator sequences its left operand before right; commas separating function arguments do not guarantee their order.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Side effect means a change to program state.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For C11, i = i++ + 1; should be classified as…

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The modification by post-increment and assignment are not safely sequenced.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with Undefined behavior.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Locate side effects such as increments and assignments.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Short circuit means skip an unnecessary right operand.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: int x=0; int ok=0 && ++x; leaves x=0 because the right side is skipped. i = i++ + 1 has undefined behavior in C11.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: It does not make undefined C behavior valid.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Use statement boundaries or specified sequencing rules.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Unsequenced means no prescribed before/after relationship.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which check avoids dereferencing a null pointer?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: && checks p first and skips dereference when p is null.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose p != NULL && *p > 0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on expression repair.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Avoid shifting signed negative values or shifting outside the operand width.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Logical result means zero or one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: What does x ^ x produce for an unsigned integer?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Each equal pair of bits cancels under exclusive OR.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is 0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave control flow and expressions, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A condition chooses which statements execute. Zero is false; any nonzero scalar value is true. An if/else selects one branch, while switch transfers to a matching case label and can fall through.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Avoid shifting signed negative values or shifting outside the operand width.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You can pause here and try the Control flow and expressions activities. Pick one idea and see whether you can explain it without the notes.

episodes.subject: c
episodes.title: Functions, builds and lifetime
episodes.description: Follow calls and distinguish scope, storage duration and linkage.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, it's Maya. I've got Leo with me for Functions, builds and lifetime.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: follow calls and distinguish scope, storage duration and linkage.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with parameters and return values and work our way to linkage and scope practice.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: parameters and return values.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Function parameters receive copied argument values. Changing a parameter does not change the caller object. A return value communicates a result; a pointer parameter can deliberately modify a caller object.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Parameter means a local object initialized from an argument.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: int add2(int x){return x+2;} called with 5 returns 7.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Assigning x=99 inside the function would change its local copy, not the caller variable.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: C passes argument values.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Passing a pointer copies the pointer value, while allowing access to the pointed-to object.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on trace nested function calls.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Follow return to resume the caller with the returned value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Argument means a supplied value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Does assigning to an int parameter alter the caller int?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: C passes argument values to parameters.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose No, the parameter is a copy.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Translation and execution are separate. Preprocessing handles directives; compilation translates a translation unit; linking resolves references between object files and libraries. A missing definition is a linking problem.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Translation unit means source after preprocessing.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: One file declares int fee(int); and calls fee(3). Another defines fee.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Both object files must participate in linking for the call to resolve.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Link object files and libraries, then run the executable.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Object file means translated code awaiting linking.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An external function is declared but no definition is linked. What usually fails?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A declaration does not provide the referenced function body.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with Linking.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Now for object lifetime and memory. What's the key distinction?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Scope controls where a name is visible; lifetime controls when its object exists; linkage connects declarations of the same entity. Automatic locals are normally new per call, while static objects last for the whole program.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Scope means where a name can be used.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: int next(void){static int x=0; return ++x;} returns 1 then 2.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A local int x=0 without static would restart at zero on every call.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Freeing storage does not automatically clear every alias.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A static local is initialized once and retains its value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Storage duration means how long storage exists.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which property says where a name is visible?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Scope describes visibility, not lifetime.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An extern declaration can refer to an object defined elsewhere.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Linkage means whether declarations refer to the same entity.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A static local survives…

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Its object has static storage duration.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is Between calls for the duration of the program.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to external names and definitions. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Compatible external declarations can refer to a single object defined in another translation unit. An extern declaration without an initializer is a declaration, while an initializer makes it a definition. Block scope does not itself imply short lifetime.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which line supplies a definition with an initializer?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The initialized file-scope object declaration is a definition.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with int total = 4;.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Separate visibility, lifetime and linkage.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: File A contains int total=4;. File B declares extern int total; and increments it.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Both names refer to the same object when the files are linked correctly.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Compatible external declarations can refer to a single object defined in another translation unit.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: File A defines total; file B uses a compatible extern declaration. How many shared total objects are intended?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: External linkage connects the declarations to the same entity.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose One.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain linkage and scope practice to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Compatible external declarations can refer to a single object defined in another translation unit.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A name can have block scope and refer to which lifetime?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Scope and storage duration answer different questions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is Static storage duration through extern.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave functions, builds and lifetime, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Function parameters receive copied argument values. Changing a parameter does not change the caller object. A return value communicates a result; a pointer parameter can deliberately modify a caller object.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Compatible external declarations can refer to a single object defined in another translation unit.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A useful next step is to revisit linkage and scope practice with an example of your own. Keep it small enough to check by hand.

episodes.subject: c
episodes.title: Recursion and the call stack
episodes.description: Descend to a base case and combine return values.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome to CSQuest Audio. I'm Maya, here with Leo. This section is called Recursion and the call stack.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: descend to a base case and combine return values.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with meet recursive calls and work our way to recursion challenges.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on meet recursive calls.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem. Each active call has its own parameters and automatic locals. A base case stops descent; return values then combine while calls unwind.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Base case means a result requiring no further recursion.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: sum(3) returns 3 + sum(2), then 2 + sum(1), then 1 + sum(0).

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: With sum(0)=0, returns combine to 6.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Each call has its own automatic locals.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain return through a call stack to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Check the base case before making the recursive call.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Call frame means one active invocation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: What is the job of a base case?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Without a reachable stopping case, descent may never terminate.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose Stop further recursion with a direct result.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Branching recursion makes separate subcalls. Repeated arguments still create separate invocations unless results are cached. Trace the full call tree and combine both results without assuming one shared parameter object.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Unwinding means resuming callers after returns.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: With f(0)=1 and f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-1), f(2) has seven calls in total and returns 4.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Repeated subproblems increase work.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Unwind returns from the smallest case to the original call.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Do two active recursive calls share the same automatic int parameter object?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Each invocation has its own automatic objects.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with No.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave recursion and the call stack, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem. Each active call has its own parameters and automatic locals. A base case stops descent; return values then combine while calls unwind.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Unwind returns from the smallest case to the original call.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We've covered a lot in recursion and the call stack. You don't have to remember every detail at once; start by trying one of the examples yourself.

episodes.subject: c
episodes.title: Pointers and arrays
episodes.description: Follow aliases, index arrays and respect pointer bounds.
topics: Size of an object or type

chapters.title: Size of an object or type

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, I'm Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Pointers and arrays.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: follow aliases, index arrays and respect pointer bounds.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with addresses and pointer arrows and work our way to array parameters and lengths.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain addresses and pointer arrows to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A pointer stores a value designating an object. & obtains an object's address; * accesses the pointed-to object. Copying a pointer creates another route to the same object, not a new copy of that object.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Address means a value designating storage.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: int x=4; int *p=&x; *p=9; changes x to 9.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Later p=&y changes what p designates without copying y into x.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An address is not the stored value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A pointer must refer to a live compatible object before dereferencing.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack modify objects through aliases next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Draw a pointer arrow to the live object it designates.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Dereference means access the object through a pointer.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: What does &x produce?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The address operator designates the existing object.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose A pointer to x.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A write through *p changes that object; assigning p changes the arrow.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Alias means another route to the same object.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which operation writes through a pointer?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: *p is the designated object, assuming p is valid and the object is writable.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is *p = 7;.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An array holds a fixed number of contiguous elements of one type. Index zero is first; an array of n elements ends at n-1. In most expressions an array becomes a pointer to its first element, but sizeof an actual array measures the whole array.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Element means one array object slot.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For int a[5], which last index is valid?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Five elements have indices zero through four.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 4.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with array update challenges. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Keep the actual array type distinct from a function's adjusted pointer parameter.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Index means an offset starting at zero.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: int a[3]={2,4,6}; a[1]=9; leaves {2,9,6}. sizeof a / sizeof a[0] is 3 in the scope where a is an actual array.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Write the valid index range.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Decay means conversion from an array expression to its first-element pointer.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: In most expressions, a for int a[5] converts to…

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Array-to-pointer conversion designates the first element.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose A pointer to a[0].

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: sizeof yields a size in bytes with type size_t. sizeof(char) is always one, but bytes need not be eight bits. For non-variable-length operands it does not evaluate the operand; a function array parameter has pointer size.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: sizeof means operator yielding a type or object size.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: int x=5; sizeof(x++); leaves x=5 for this non-VLA operand. int a[4]; has four times sizeof(int) bytes.

turns.speaker: leo

turns.text: Now for pointer arithmetic challenges. What's the key distinction?

turns.speaker: leo

turns.speaker: maya
